The 2014 parse had an offset answer key and fused options, so every key was re-derived; six keys were corrected (demand shift, supply-function quantity, fixed costs, stagflation, money market, quota). Figure-dependent, ambiguous and unrecoverable rows were rejected and are listed in docs/deferred.md.
subject: economics

questions.question: A change in demand for a normal good implies that there is ______.

options.text: a shift in the demand curve
a change in the quantity demanded as price changes
a movement along a given demand curve
a change in the price elasticity of demand

questions.explanation: A change in demand means the whole relationship has changed, so the curve shifts. A change in the good’s own price causes a movement along the existing curve.

questions.question: Given the supply function P = ¼(Qs + 10), when P = N10, Qs is ______.
questions.explanation: Substitute P = 10: 10 = ¼(Qs + 10). Multiply both sides by 4 to get 40 = Qs + 10, so Qs = 30.

questions.question: The price mechanism determines the prices of commodities through ______.
questions.explanation: In a market economy, the interaction of demand and supply — market forces — sets price. Treasury bills and legislation are not price-setting mechanisms for goods.

questions.question: Rent and administrative expenses are examples of ______.
questions.explanation: Rent and administrative salaries are paid even when output is zero, so they are fixed costs. Average fixed cost is a per-unit figure, not the cost itself.

questions.question: If the marginal propensity to consume is 2/3 and investment is N100 million, the level of national income is ______.
questions.explanation: The multiplier is 1 ÷ (1 − MPC) = 1 ÷ (1/3) = 3. National income = 3 × N100 million = N300 million.

questions.question: Inflation that co-exists with a high rate of unemployment is called ______.
questions.explanation: Stagflation combines rising prices with stagnant output and high unemployment. Demand-pull and cost-push inflation describe causes, not the unemployment combination.

questions.question: Short-term loans for investment are usually obtained through the ______.
questions.explanation: The money market handles short-term funds such as treasury bills and commercial paper. The capital market and development banks supply medium- and long-term finance.

questions.question: A wage freeze is a policy measure aimed at ______.
questions.explanation: A wage freeze holds down labour costs and disposable income, which slows cost-push and demand-pull pressure on prices. It is an anti-inflation measure.

questions.question: A major feature of an underdeveloped economy is ______.

options.text: a low level of standard of living
a low rate of population growth

questions.explanation: Underdeveloped economies are characterised by low income per head and therefore a low standard of living, alongside low capital formation and high underemployment.

questions.question: An important role of agriculture in an economy is ______.
questions.explanation: Agriculture employs a large share of the labour force and supplies food and raw materials. Processing raw materials is manufacturing, not farming.

questions.question: An advantage of large-scale farming over peasant farming is ______.

options.text: encouraging the use of traditional implements
conducting research and employing labour on a large scale

questions.explanation: Large-scale farms can afford research, machinery and specialised labour, which raise yields. Traditional implements and income redistribution are not advantages of scale.

questions.question: One major factor that determines the location of an industry is ______.

options.text: the capital base of the firm
the social responsibility of the firm

questions.explanation: Firms locate near markets to cut transport costs and reach customers, especially when the product is bulky or perishable. Capital base affects scale, not location.

questions.question: The major contribution of OPEC to the Nigerian economy is the provision of ______.
questions.explanation: OPEC coordinates production among oil-exporting countries to stabilise prices. It does not build infrastructure, pay subsidies or refine crude oil.

questions.question: The short-run average variable cost of a firm will rise owing to ______.

options.text: an increase in the cost of labour
the building of a new warehouse
an increase in the salaries of directors

questions.explanation: Variable costs change with output, and labour is a variable input. Factory space, warehouses and directors’ salaries are fixed costs in the short run.

questions.question: Firms embark on vertical integration in order to ______.

options.text: take over markets formerly controlled by other firms
prevent other firms from entering the market

questions.explanation: Vertical integration combines stages of production or distribution, which can lower costs and secure supply. Taking over a competitor’s market is horizontal integration.

questions.question: A trade control measure that limits imports to a definite quantity is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A quota sets a physical limit on the quantity imported. A tariff is a tax on imports, and an excise duty is a tax on domestic production.
